purpose.statement: Provide a deterministic, provider-neutral orchestration runtime that turns approved goals into accepted software through explicit modular engineering contracts, evidence, gates, and traceable lifecycle progression.

businessObjectives.statement: Make software-engineering progression reproducible and fail closed when required inputs, evidence, or approvals are invalid.
Allow best-in-class engineering capabilities to be replaced without changing canonical workflow semantics or generic Core.
Make every DevRelay run understandable and measurable to a human across any configured number of modules, Gates, adapters, retries, and parallel frontiers.

businessObjectives.statement: Require scoped verification and evidence before work, changes, systems, or business outcomes advance.
Trace every approved business objective through requirements, design, planned work, implementation, verification, integration, and acceptance.
Prevent invalid, cyclic, incomplete, or impossible dependency plans from reaching assignment and execution.
Replace dependency-analysis capabilities without changing canonical semantics or generic Core.
Provide authoritative ordering sufficient for downstream systems to identify safely runnable work.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Every dependency hint receives exactly one evidence-backed disposition.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: WorkDependencyGate rejects invalid endpoints, duplicate edges, contradictory evidence, OPA-denied relationships, unresolved reviewer findings, and other policy-forbidden ordering.

acceptanceCriteria.verification: Attempt adapter graph operations, then verify projection, merge proof, replay, retirement, and approved authority.

risks: A consistency reviewer may be mistaken for authority unless reviewer findings remain advisory inputs to the Gate.
A human-readable report may become misleading if missing measurements are silently treated as zero.
A reporting service may accidentally acquire workflow authority unless its read-only boundary is enforced.
Adapter performance comparisons may be invalid when inputs, policies, hosts, or circuit versions differ.
Adapter-native semantics may leak into canonical contracts unless conformance remains strict.
Ambiguous edge direction could duplicate inverse facts.
Analyzer silence could be mistaken for proof that no dependency is missing.
Compatibility claims can be wrong if compared against a stale ContractBaseline.
Conditional routing may become implicit unless every condition remains state-driven and evidence-bound.
Context slices may omit a semantically relevant source region unless Gate coverage checks remain independent of proposer selection.
Contract-format special cases in Core could prevent module and tool replacement.
Frontier completion may unlock dependent work too early unless only verified integrated-completion facts affect readiness.
Gate proliferation may add friction unless quick paths remain clear and policy is risk-adjusted.
Generator self-certification could admit malformed or semantically incomplete contracts.
Graphology traversal or serialization order may leak nondeterminism unless Core canonicalizes all externally visible artifacts and diagnostics.
Hidden adapter-selected context could violate deterministic invocation contracts.
Module boundaries may drift into duplicated responsibility unless every contract keeps one primary purpose.
OPA policy success may be mistaken for semantic completeness unless WorkDependencyGate separately reviews missing-dependency evidence.
Operational telemetry may leak secrets or sensitive logs unless report projection applies explicit content policy.
Reused task adapters could blur decomposition and dependency authority.
Stored execution waves could couple static dependencies to changing runtime state.
Traceability may become incomplete when future contributors omit required lifecycle relationships or evidence horizons.
WorkBreakdown can propagate invalid scope if it starts before ContractGate resolution.
